beats.headline: The last entry in the back
beats.text: Crawler Carl cannot sleep, and a passage from the back of the Cookbook keeps coming back to him. It was written by a crawler named York, author of the tenth edition, who wrote pages and pages of rambling philosophical essays Carl can barely follow. This one appears to be his last entry. I have been surrounded by my hive, yet I have been alone, it says. The Cookbook, York writes, is an attempt to make a hive of those who never cross paths, except in these pages. And there is consolation in dying in the pursuit of justice, however small.

beats.headline: A mantis on the eighth floor
beats.text: From a season long past, when the crawl was run by the Reavers. The eighth level that season was mountains connected by wires and gondolas. The crawlers were a strange type of mantis, not the common kind, who could not fly and did poorly in the cold. There was a crawler among them named York, and an NPC named Dante, who had once left a single entry in the Cookbook himself, was watching him carefully.

beats.headline: Read by the next one
beats.text: A note added by crawler Ikicha, eleventh edition. Ikicha's kind are castrated and cast out, a perspective as different as could be from the one who came before: York, who appears to have come from a hive, yet says he always felt alone his entire life. Reading his words, Ikicha feels kinship anyway, and asks the question on the page. Did he survive? Then a prayer that anyone who gets free seeks out those who came before.

beats.headline: The yacht, if he does his duty
beats.text: Filed from Rosetta's side of the deal. In exchange for a pin number, the Pacifist Network agreed to destroy an orc yacht with several children aboard, and with Stalwart dead, one of those children is the new king of the Skull Empire. The job falls to York, in orbit. Rosetta's assessment: assuming he actually does his duty and does not decide to write a poem instead. She also names York among those she hopes survive whatever comes next.

beats.headline: Point defense, and nothing felt
beats.text: York, tenodera, the only living creature aboard the Homecoming Queen, the largest ship in orbit, with more guns than anyone knows about and enhancement zone weapons Porthus had installed. When everyone started shooting at each other, York vaporised the orc yacht with a point defense beam. Everyone assumes crossfire. He had looked forward to it: he wanted to feel something afterwards. He did not. He writes verse about it, crumples the verse, and writes another. He suspects all his poems are terrible.

beats.headline: The crawl he remembers
beats.text: His entire hive entered the dungeon, and he vaguely recalls the anger as they were picked off one by one, and the realisation that he never fit in. Around the ninth floor a numbness spread, which he puts down to his tenodera blood: warriors bred for the job of killing an enemy hive's children. The card, for the record: Advocate. Top level 71. Took a deal at the end of the tenth floor. Game Guide and Guildhall Instructor in the Poetry guild. Author of the tenth edition. Current status: captain in the Open Intellect Action Network.

beats.headline: At that moment, something
beats.text: Boomer comes on the screen as the Homecoming Queen docks to load soldiers, and asks the usual question: written any new poems? Any good? All his poetry is good, York says. Boomer's own poem is about winning Faction Wars and killing more of them. That is a terrible poem, Boomer. The breaching suits are ready, York reports, and the enhancement zone suits and power armour are online, just as Porthus predicted. Boomer says it is time to bring the war out of the dungeon. At that moment, York does, indeed, feel something.
